characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Zeiss Supra 55 FEG-SEM equipped with EDS and Nordley EBSD detectors (Oxford)
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn0Ni IPF map at 1173 K shows very large single-colour domains indicating pronounced grain growth; the alloy is single-phase (B2-free). Recrystallization fraction reaches 1.0, recrystallized grain size ~40 μm, twin fraction just under 0.6 and B2 fraction 0.0 at 1173 K.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Step size of 120 nm (fine-grained) / 250 nm (coarse-grained) on ~100×100 μm² and ~200×200 μm² areas; three scans per sample; data analyzed with TSL-OIM software
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine grain orientations, grain size, twin fraction (Σ3 CSL boundaries), recrystallization fraction (KAM/GOS <2° criteria), and phase distribution in the HR+CR+1173 K condition

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku XRD instrument with Co-Kα radiation at 45 kV and 135 mA, beam size ~2 mm
characterization_methods.key_findings: The XRD pattern of 28Mn0Ni alloy heat treated at 1173 K showed peaks corresponding to γ-phase only (κ-carbide and B2 peaks present at 973 K disappeared).
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases present in cold rolled and heat-treated conditions

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: FEI TECNAI 20T G2 TEM operating at 200 kV equipped with EDAX EDS; specimens twin-jet electropolished in mixed acid at 243 K (−30 °C)
characterization_methods.key_findings: No secondary phase precipitates were seen in 28Mn0Ni alloy at 1173 K (Fig. 7a and b); large austenite grain with straight angular planar bands and no resolvable second-phase particles.
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phases, precipitates and deformation substructure not resolved at SEM-EBSD scale

characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn0Ni in HR+CR+1173 K: YS 504 ± 5 MPa, UTS 905 ± 8 MPa, TE 86 ± 2 %, n = 0.50 — highest ductility and strain hardening among the tested conditions.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, constant cross-head speed 0.5 mm/min (initial strain rate ~3×10^-4 s^-1); gauge length 30 mm, width 6 mm, thickness 4–5 mm; ASTM E8M
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate strength and ductility of the chosen alloys in different processing conditions
characterization_methods.technique: Uniaxial tensile testing (and interrupted tensile testing)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AFFRI Vickers hardness tester, peak load 30 kg (~300 N), dwell time 15 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: 28Mn0Ni hardness decreases monotonically with heat treatment temperature and is lower than the Ni-containing alloys at every temperature; the drop in hardness with temperature was most prominent in the Ni-free alloy, falling to below 200 VHN at 1273 K.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Bulk hardness as per ASTM E-140-02; averaged over ten measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Evaluate hardness variation with degree of cold work and heat treatment temperature

characterization_methods.key_findings: Fractography of 28Mn0Ni tensile specimens (HR+CR+1023 K example reported) exhibited dimple morphology, indicating ductile failure; consistent with the observed high ductility.
characterization_methods.purpose: Understand fracture mode of failed tensile specimens
characterization_methods.technique: Scanning electron microscopy fractography (and post-tensile deformed microstructure)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: In fully recrystallized and precipitate-free austenite grains of 28Mn0Ni (HR+CR+1173 K), progressive substructure evolution occurred with applied strain: dislocation multiplication → planar slip → dynamic slip band refinement; dislocation-twin interaction (with prior annealing twins) was observed as a dominant strain-hardening mechanism.

interfaces.interface_notes: No γ/B2 interphase boundaries survive at 1173 K in 28Mn0Ni since the alloy is B2-free in this condition.
interfaces.phase_evolution: After heating to 1173 K the 28Mn0Ni alloy reverts to single-phase γ only: κ-carbide/B2 that appeared at 973 K are dissolved; no secondary-phase peaks remain in XRD at 1173 K and no precipitates seen by TEM.
interfaces.slip_behavior: Planar slip activity followed by dynamic slip band refinement in the fully recrystallized austenite; in 28Mn0Ni (1173 K), homogeneous slip band spacing. Slip band evolution from sparse planar slip (ε~0.02) through slip-band refinement (ε~0.08, 0.30) to dislocation interaction with prior annealing twins.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Sound portion of the 30 kg vacuum-induction-melted ingot was homogenized at 1423 K for 2.5 h.
Hot rolled at 1323 K; final thickness of hot rolled plate about 13 mm. This condition is referred to as HR. Details reported elsewhere [21].
Cold rolled to ~50% reduction in thickness (~6 mm thick sheets) by several passes; the 28Mn0Ni alloy rolled successfully without cracking at room temperature till 50% reduction.

processing_steps.method: heat treatment (annealing) followed by water quenching
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cold rolled sheets were heat treated in the temperature range 873 K–1273 K for 1 h followed by water quenching; for this sample the temperature was 1173 K.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests were triplicated for each condition and the average of three readings was reported.
measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Flat tensile specimens with a gauge length of 30 mm, width 6 mm and thickness 4–5 mm

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of 28Mn0Ni-1173 K (solid black) reaches the largest strain (~0.85) at the lowest stress level (~900 MPa); true stress-true strain for 28Mn0Ni-1173 K is the lowest and rises most gradually to ~1500 MPa near 0.55 true strain.

structures.microstructure_counts: Recrystallized austenite fraction = 1.0; twin fraction just under 0.6; B2 volume fraction = 0.0 at 1173 K.

phases_present.morphology: equiaxed, coarse grained; very large single-colour domains indicating pronounced grain growth

structures.overall_structure: Fully recrystallized austenite with significant grain growth; single-phase γ (FCC), B2-free; no secondary phase precipitates resolvable after heat treatment at 1173 K.

unmapped_findings: For 28Mn0Ni (Fe–28Mn–9Al-0.9C) in HR+CR+1173 K, the alloy is fully recrystallized with significant grain growth (recrystallized austenite grain size ~40 μm, error bar ~30–50 μm), recrystallization fraction = 1.0, twin fraction just under 0.6, and secondary B2 phase volume fraction = 0.0 (Fig. 5).

Vickers hardness of 28Mn0Ni after 1173 K heat treatment is lower than the Ni-containing alloys at the same temperature and shows the most prominent drop with temperature among the three alloys (exact value at 1173 K not reported numerically in the text/figure description).

The 28Mn0Ni alloy in HR+CR+1173 K reached the best strength-ductility combination (YS ~500 MPa, UTS ~1000 MPa, TE ~86%) consistent with prior annealing studies in the single-phase region; the processing temperature window for 28Mn0Ni was inferred to be around 973 K, not 1173 K.

High strain hardening ability of the fully recrystallized 28Mn0Ni (HR+CR+1173 K) is associated with planar slip activity followed by dynamic slip band refinement (and dislocation-twin interaction with prior annealing twins) with a homogeneous slip band spacing.
In HR+CR condition, 28Mn0Ni exhibited YS 1350 ± 10 MPa, UTS 1500 ± 10 MPa, TE 10 ± 0.4 % (no n value), showing cold rolling gives high strength/low ductility before the 1173 K heat treatment.
28Mn0Ni in HR condition had an initial hardness of ~256 ± 5 VHN; hardness saturated to around 450 VHN at 50% cold reduction in all three alloys.
